hints: Look closely at the reaction conditions for each option, acidic and oxidising versus alkaline, as they decide the final form of the product.
Remember that ethanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CN}$, can be hydrolysed in both acid and alkali, but only one gives the free acid directly.
Think about what happens to a carboxylic acid in sodium hydroxide solution, and spot which reaction leaves the product as a salt.
walkthrough:
**Recall the oxidation routes to acids**

Both ethanol and ethanal can be oxidised to ethanoic acid when heated under reflux with acidified dichromate(VI). Reflux ensures full oxidation, not stopping at ethanal.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + 2[O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + [O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$

**Recall the two types of nitrile hydrolysis**

Ethanenitrile hydrolyses on heating with aqueous acid to give ethanoic acid directly, plus an ammonium salt. With aqueous alkali it gives the carboxylate salt plus ammonia.

Acid hydrolysis:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CN} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$

Alkaline hydrolysis:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CN} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^- + \text{NH}_3$$

**Pick the one that does not give the free acid**

In dilute sodium hydroxide, the product is sodium ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$, not ethanoic acid. You would need a separate acidification step to get the acid. So this is the reaction that would not give ethanoic acid.

options.A: Heating ethanenitrile with dilute NaOH gives alkaline hydrolysis to sodium ethanoate and ammonia. Because the solution is alkaline, the organic product stays as the ethanoate ion, $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$, and free ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, is not formed.
options.B: Heating ethanenitrile with dilute sulfuric acid gives acid hydrolysis to ethanoic acid and ammonium hydrogensulfate. This does give ethanoic acid, so it is not the answer.
options.C: Ethan al is an aldehyde and is easily oxidised by acidified dichromate(VI) under reflux to ethanoic acid. Students sometimes confuse reflux with distillation, but reflux gives the full oxidation to the acid.
options.D: Ethanol is a primary alcohol and is fully oxidised to ethanoic acid when heated under reflux with excess acidified dichromate(VI). Distillation would stop at ethanal, but reflux drives it all the way to the acid.
